messages.author: bcc0e0575e2050f2
messages.subject: Use of ObsNum function in Unmarked
parts:
Hi All,

Hope you are well.

This may seem like a silly question. Looking at the sample text below from the Pcount function. Could I use the ObsNum function in place of the observation level covariates in order to estimate the population size of a species using camera trap count data?


data(mallard)
mallardUMF <- unmarkedFramePCount(mallard.y, siteCovs = mallard.site,
obsCovs = mallard.obs)
(fm.mallard <- pcount(~ ivel+ date + I(date^2) ~ length + elev + forest, mallardUMF, K=30))
(fm.mallard.nb <- pcount(~ date + I(date^2) ~ length + elev, mixture = "NB", mallardUMF, K=30))
(fm1re <- ranef(fm1))
plot(fm1re, subset=site %in% 1:25, xlim=c(-1,40))
sum(bup(fm1re))         # Estimated population size
sum(N)                  # Actual population size

Thanks for your time and help.

Kind regards,
Tristan

messages.subject: Re: Use of ObsNum function in Unmarked
parts:
I included ObsNum due to dates not fitting the data well. My worry now is that the using ObsNum makes the analysis circular, i.e. more captures equates to higher detections.

Please could someone explain how ObsNum is integrated into the model?

Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,
Tristan

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Use of ObsNum function in Unmarked
parts:
Dear Tristan,

I don't know what the ObsNum function is. But it should not be impossible to use an Nmix model (i.e., function pcount in unmarked) to estimate population size under the following two main assumptions:
  • You must be able to identify the individuals sufficiently well to exclude any double, triple .... counts of the same individual for a given occasion and trap. That is, a count such as, say, 5 must mean that there were exactly 5 unique individuals that appear in any number of photographs during the time period that you chose to define as an 'occasion'. You must be able to exclude the possibility that the first count was 4 individuals, of which one was photographed twice etc.
  • In addition, every detected individual must only occur at a single trap.
The main caveat then will be that your "abundance estimate" will in a sense still only be a sort of detection-corrected index, because the Nmix model is not a spatially explicit model. You don't know the areas associated with each trap, from which the observed individuals were drawn. Therefore, you will not be able to convert your abundance estimate into an estimate of density, or only under strong and untestable assumptions. Such as when you claim that all animals potentially detectable at a trap must come from some distance not further away than T, where T is chosen by you.

Best regards  --- Marc

I think that if one wants to use the total count (btw, I assume this would be total number of pictures made during an occasion at a trap) as a detection covariate, then one would first have to subtract the number of pictures for the target species.

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Use of ObsNum function in Unmarked
parts:
Hi guys,

I'm not sure if this is related, but unmarked internally creates an observation covariate called 'obsNum' that you can include in the detection part of the model to get occasion-specific estimates of detection parameters (like model Mt in mark-recapture):

> library(unmarked)
> example(unmarked)
> occu(~obsNum ~1, umf)

Call:
occu(formula = ~obsNum ~ 1, data = umf)

Occupancy:
 Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
     -1.1 0.231 -4.74 2.16e-06

Detection:
            Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)    0.235 0.403 0.584  0.5593
obsNum2        0.510 0.587 0.869  0.3847
obsNum3        0.164 0.573 0.286  0.7749
obsNum4        0.700 0.599 1.168  0.2428
obsNum5        1.407 0.676 2.081  0.0374

AIC: 275.2603


This isn't documented very well, and most people do this manually by creating a matrix to indicate the occasion number associated with each observation.

--
Richard Chandler
Associate Professor
Wildlife Ecology and Conservation
Warnell School of Forestry and Natural Resources
University of Georgia
762-499-4085
http://chandlerlab.uga.edu/

obsCovs = mallard.obs)

I'm not sure if this is related, but unmarked internally creates an observation covariate called 'obsNum' that you can include in the detection part of the model to get occasion-specific estimates of detection parameters (like model Mt in mark-recapture):

On Fri, 12 Nov 2021, 16:48 Marc Kery, <marc...@vogelwarte.ch> wrote:
Dear Tristan,

I don't know what the ObsNum function is. But it should not be impossible to use an Nmix model (i.e., function pcount in unmarked) to estimate population size under the following two main assumptions:
  • You must be able to identify the individuals sufficiently well to exclude any double, triple .... counts of the same individual for a given occasion and trap. That is, a count such as, say, 5 must mean that there were exactly 5 unique individuals that appear in any number of photographs during the time period that you chose to define as an 'occasion'. You must be able to exclude the possibility that the first count was 4 individuals, of which one was photographed twice etc.
  • In addition, every detected individual must only occur at a single trap.
The main caveat then will be that your "abundance estimate" will in a sense still only be a sort of detection-corrected index, because the Nmix model is not a spatially explicit model. You don't know the areas associated with each trap, from which the observed individuals were drawn. Therefore, you will not be able to convert your abundance estimate into an estimate of density, or only under strong and untestable assumptions. Such as when you claim that all animals potentially detectable at a trap must come from some distance not further away than T, where T is chosen by you.

Best regards  --- Marc
